name: Invoice Capture and Coding
title: Invoice Capture and Coding
answer: Invoice capture and coding covers the intake of supplier invoices from email, scan, or electronic feed and the conversion of those documents into structured records. It includes reading header fields such as vendor name, invoice number, date, and total, and line items such as description, quantity, unit price, and tax. The coding part assigns each line or the whole invoice to general ledger accounts, cost centers, projects, or other dimensions used by the accounting system. It also covers matching to purchase orders and receipts, flagging duplicates, and routing exceptions for review. This work sits inside accounts payable and feeds directly into the general ledger and payment run.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Invoice capture and coding covers the intake of supplier invoices from email, scan, or electronic feed and the conversion of those documents into structured records. It includes reading header fields such as vendor name, invoice number, date, and total, and line items such as description, quantity, unit price, and tax. The coding part assigns each line or the whole invoice to general ledger accounts, cost centers, projects, or other dimensions used by the accounting system. It also covers matching to purchase orders and receipts, flagging duplicates, and routing exceptions for review. This work sits inside accounts payable and feeds directly into the general ledger and payment run.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on a stack that starts with document ingestion from email inboxes, shared folders, scanners, or supplier portals. Optical character recognition and layout analysis turn page images into text and positional data, and machine learning models then classify the document and extract fields. These services are often cloud based, with connectors into ERP and accounting systems such as SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, or QuickBooks for posting and matching. Some deployments keep processing on premises for data residency or control reasons, while others use a hybrid model. The output is a structured record that the payables system can validate, code, and route.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The method usually begins with classification, separating invoices from statements, credit notes, and other documents. Extraction then pulls the fields, often using a mix of template rules for known layouts and learned models for unseen ones. Coding can be rule based, for example mapping a vendor to a default expense account, or learned from historical coding decisions and purchase order data. Validation checks totals, tax calculations, and vendor master data, and any low confidence result goes to a human reviewer. Straight through processing rates depend on document quality, vendor consistency, and how well the coding rules cover the spend.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk in invoice capture and coding centre on financial control, data protection, and auditability. The extracted data and the coding decisions must be traceable, so systems keep an audit trail of who or what changed a field and when. Provenance matters for models as well, including which training data was used and which model version produced a result. Risks include mis-coded expenses, duplicate payments, missed early payment discounts, and fraud through altered bank details or fake invoices. Compliance obligations can include retention rules, access controls, and financial reporting standards, and vendor contracts should set out data processing terms.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward fewer manual touches and more continuous coding as invoices arrive. Large language models are being applied to messy, unstructured invoices that older extraction methods handled poorly, and coding is increasingly suggested in real time rather than in a batch. Integration with payment rails and e-invoicing networks is deepening, which brings capture and coding closer to the moment of transaction. Controls are shifting from periodic review to embedded checks that run on every invoice. The likely result is a smaller exception queue and a greater share of invoices posted without human intervention.
